reviews.comment: Waer lectures well and gave me a decent understanding of the material. I was able to get through all of the hw assignments okay for the most part. The final exam was much harder than the review as well as the hw from all semester. As long as you perform well on the labs, you should be able to perform poorly on the final and still escape with a B.

The final is crazy hard so do well on labs & the hw to make up for failing the final. Fine enough prof during lectures, most people stop showing up mid way thru the semester. hw is also difficult so work on it when you first get it. labs are ok, you can get by if you follow what the graphs should look like and use the rubric. good luck!

By far my favorite professor in A&M. He's caring and genuinely wants to get along with his students while also teaching very well. If you don't understand lectures go to his office hours. Do the hw, participate in class and do the labs and you'll be fine.

Loved this prof, engaging lectures for not very engaging material. Gives out less work compared to other 216 profs, which was awesome for my workload. The end of the material is heavily physics based, and so are all the labs, so don't slack in 206 and you should be more than okay in this class. I recommend this prof over any other 216 prof!!

Waer's a very solid prof for ENGR/PHYS 216. He goes on tangents often but he likes to keep the class engaged. He'll love you if you watch Monty Python and the Holy Grail and can get his jokes. The final was hard but isn't heavily weighted. Attend all lectures despite non-mandatory. Before final, review all lecture slides, including definitions.

The class is easy if you just do great on the homework and the labs. There are lots of extra credit opportunities so pay attention in his class to earn points.  I liked his little jokes in lectures about mostly Monty Python and the Holy Grail. Definitely don't be afraid to ask for help. Cooperate with lab partners as well. Do practice hw questions.

Overall a good professor. Just do good on he homework and labs. Then, for the final, look over the lecture slides and do practice problems. The final is what gets many people, so just do enough practice questions before the final.

Professor Waer is hilarious. He likes to joke and have fun in class. He gets you the information you need to know, and the grading on the assignments is very relaxed, given that the class is heavily weighted towards the lab time. The final exam was hard, the class average was a 55, but it was only worth 20% of the grade, so not too big of a deal.

Professor Waer is a decent and jovial teacher. He has great professional experience and academic insight, have a chat with him! The course is a mixture of physics, math and engineering. Do well on labs and homework (3/4 of the grade). There is some extra credit (1%). Material could've been taught better. Overall, I recommend Waer for 216.

He is a really fair teacher, if he goes over the end time, he will give extra points based on how many minutes he goes over. So if class ends at 5 and he keeps the class to 5:02 he will give 2 points on the upcoming assignment.
I love this man with all my heart, ALL OF IT!!

Waer is a very nice man who cares about his students and is passionate about what he teaches. Lecture is a little boring but he tries to make it interactive. There is homework due once every 2 weeks and a final. The rest of your grade comes from the labs. I got a 30 on the final and still got a B, if that tells you anything about the curve.

Nice guy. Tries to joke around and make lectures entertaining, the material is just so dry it's hard to keep people engaged. Homework can be hard/tedious but nothing unreasonable. Responds quickly and fully to emails. Literally everybody in my section failed the final, but he have the class a hefty curve in return. Solid choice for PHYS 216 overall

I guess I only had 2 complaints about him. The first being he never graded anything during the semester and we really only knew our grade in the class after he put it all into HOWDY, the second would be that his lectures and homework were never really on the same page and you kinda had to do some digging to do some of the questions.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really nice and funny prof, but at the times the homework could be difficult as they sometimes strayed away from lecture material. Labs are run completely by TAs and are very time consuming. Only one exam (the final), and it's only worth a small portion of the grade. Do the HW and labs carefully and you should get an A. Gives lots of extra credit

Just truly got the sense he did not care to help you in anyway possible. The only assignment for labs are the lab reports and we all know they grade very difficult on those. Plus, the lab is 56% of your whole grade. Like who does that ???? At least add other assignments to the lab class if the lab portions weighs that much for the class as a whole.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great dude, lectures get old and boring though, and he does assign homework from them. He tries to keep everyone attentive but it's just the material. He is a professor of practice as well. Has some cool stories from the Navy. He is accessible outside of class for the homework and helps a bit. He will make you work for an A, but its obtainable

I think Richard is a great guy, who really cares about engineering and his students. That being said, I don't think he's the best lector, with lectures not really making sense and not aligning with the homework. I honestly had to rely on Chegg to learn the material, which wasn't that hard when explained by other people. Just show up to class.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Waer is a solid choice for PHYS/ENGR216, gives very few homework assignments compared to the other professors. Just beware the final in this class is what always gets people. Luckily for my class the final was made optional, thank you china.

Waer is a solid choice for 216. His expectations are clear and as long as you fulfill them it's easy to make an A. His lectures are dull, but he personally is an interesting and funny speaker. This class kind of sucks, but Waer is a good choice for it. TA's grade everything anyways
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: He would often ramble on about random things during class, which was better than listening to a powerpoint presentation for an hour, but which basically left us to figure out the homework on our own, especially the first few. That said, he was better than most of the other professors, and seemed to care about his students a lot.

Dr. Waer cares about us learning and loves to tell stories, he's is a great guy. After we all went online because of the virus, he seemed very genuinely sad he wouldn't get to teach us face to face anymore. I found that in his class, we got less homework assignments than people with other profs. He takes attendance about half the time.

Just fyi, phys 216 and engr 216 are the same thing, and there is little to no coding involved. It's mostly a laboratory for physics, with some extra homework. Professor Waer is kind, and often gives extra time for homework or no homework at all. He has some attendance checks, but the class is so short and typically ends earlier it's worth it.
